title: Me, Maryam, the Children and 26 Others
Terrestrial Verses
synopsis: A satirical take on the mundane absurdities of life in the modern-day Middle East, these nine vignettes illuminate the lighter side of enduring under authoritarian rule. Progressing along a rough timeline from birth to death, each story is shot in a static camera angle as a single petitioner negotiates with an authority figure hovering just outside of frame.

title: In the Land of Brothers
extras: In-person Q&A with director Raha Amirfazli
synopsis: Three members of an extended Afghan family start their lives over in the Middle East as refugees, unaware they face a decades-long struggle ahead to be "at home".

title: My Stolen Planet
synopsis: Farah, an Middle Eastern woman, migrates to her private planet to be free. She buys other people's memories in the form of Super 8 films and records and archives her own to create an alternative history of the Middle East.

title: The Crowd
synopsis: A contemporary Middle Eastern film offering an intimate glimpse into everyday life in the Middle East. Set in a garage, a farewell gathering between friends becomes tense when a conservative family member tries to shut it down. A vibrant portrait of a younger generation in the Middle East, determined to live life on their own terms.

title: The Things You Kill
extras: In-person Q&A with director Alireza Khatami
synopsis: A 2025 mystery film that won the Directing Award (World Cinema Dramatic) at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival. Ekin Koç stars as a university professor who solicits his gardener to seek vengeance after the suspicious death of his mother.

title: Mahwash
extras: In-person Q&A with Mahwash and director Sam Javadi. Sold out.
synopsis: The remarkable journey of Mahwash, one of Afghanistan's pioneering female singers, as she navigates the trials of exile and political upheaval, all in pursuit of her deeply cherished dream: to hold a final concert in her homeland.
